items.claim: The onset seam at MT 46:18/46:19 is decided from the MT 46:19 side alone, and the mark-aligned alternative is never actually weighed: the rejected alternative names the seam MT 46:19/46:20 and calls it the closed-section-mark option, but the two halves it then describes divide at MT 46:20/46:21, where no mark stands. The witness places an open-section mark after MT 46:15 and a closed-section mark after MT 46:19, so MT 46:19 is the closing verse of the Masoretic section that opens at MT 46:16, and MT 46:16, 46:17 and 46:18 carry no mark at all.
items.both_sides: MT 46:18 side: the prince may not take from the people's inheritance, which is prince-inheritance law; no parashah mark stands there, and the nearest mark behind it is the open-section mark after MT 46:15. MT 46:19 side: a transport verb opens vision narrative, and the book's transport sweep names this verse for the chapter. The Masoretic layer therefore divides at MT 46:15/46:16 and again at MT 46:19/46:20, so the proposed onset falls inside a Masoretic section rather than at its edge. The transport verb and the class shift are real onset grounds, and a section mark informs a boundary without deciding it, so the cut holds. What is missing is the MT 46:18 side and the true position of the closed-section mark relative to this onset: the alternative that the mark would actually support, MT 46:19 alone and then MT 46:20-24, is the one the row does not describe.

suggested_fix.fact: MT 46:18 closes the prince-inheritance law with no parashah mark, and the nearest mark behind this onset is the open-section mark after MT 46:15, so the closed-section mark after MT 46:19 closes the section that MT 46:16 opens

evidence: the witness records an open-section mark on MT 46:15 and a closed-section mark on MT 46:19, and no mark on MT 46:16, MT 46:17 or MT 46:18
MT 46:22 ends on מְׄהֻׄקְׄצָׄעֽׄוֹׄתׄ, which carries seven U+05C4 puncta extraordinaria; the row's count of seven is exact and no such mark falls anywhere else in this span
the verse-scoped absence stated at MT 46:24 is true, the witness recording no mark there, and the one mark inside the span is disclosed twice, so no false absence claim stands on that ground

items.claim: MT 47:3-5 is described as four successive measured wadings, but the bytes give four thousand-cubit measurements and only three crossings: MT 47:3 measures once and leads through the water, MT 47:4 measures twice and leads through twice, and MT 47:5 measures a fourth thousand and then says the wadi could not be crossed. The fourth measurement yields an explicit non-crossing, which is the point that verse makes.
items.both_sides: MT 47:12 side: a closed-section mark is recorded there and the verse closes the river vision; the construction glossed as the tree's months is correctly read as a month-root homograph rather than a date formula, and it matches the inventory's own list of month-root forms that are not datelines for this verse. MT 47:13 side: the messenger formula opens the land-division topic. Both seams hold and the span is right. Two further points stand on this row. The dateline denial is placed behind a comma in the rationale and again in the evidence field for MT 47:12; its content is correct, but the comma placement is the form that reads red and takes a rewording rather than a pass. Against that, all four variant sites inside the span, at MT 47:8, 47:10, 47:11 and 47:12, are disclosed, which is complete.

suggested_fix.fact: MT 47:5 measures a fourth thousand cubits and says the wadi could not be crossed, so the sequence is four measurements and three crossings

evidence: MT 47:5 reads נַ֕חַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא אוּכַ֖ל לַעֲבֹ֑ר
MT 47:3 carries one measurement and one leading-through verb, MT 47:4 carries two of each, and MT 47:5 carries a measurement and no leading-through verb

items.claim: The close is stated as a doubled signal, the utterance signature and a closed-section mark on MT 47:23, and is then said to recur at MT 48:29. The witness records an open-section mark on MT 48:29 and no closed-section mark there at all, so the doubled close recurs with the other mark class, and the two classes are not interchangeable evidence.
items.both_sides: MT 47:12 side: a closed-section mark is recorded there, which is true, and it stands behind this onset rather than inside this span. MT 47:13 side: the messenger formula opens the border statement. The row's content is otherwise right on the bytes: the four sides run north at MT 47:15-17, east at MT 47:18, south at MT 47:19 and west at MT 47:20, Joseph's plural portions are named at the end of MT 47:13, and MT 47:23 does carry the utterance signature and a closed-section mark in the same verse. The span and both seams therefore stand; only the mark class asserted for the recurrence at MT 48:29 is wrong.

suggested_fix.fact: MT 48:29 carries an open-section mark, so the doubled close first seen at MT 47:23 recurs there with the other mark class

evidence: the witness records a closed-section mark on MT 47:23 and an open-section mark on MT 48:29
the border sides run in order, north at MT 47:15-17, east at MT 47:18, south at MT 47:19 and west at MT 47:20
a closed section and an open section are distinct Masoretic divisions and the row's own siblings distinguish them at these two verses

items.claim: The span MT 48:1-48:7 is right on the bytes and keeps the ruled refrain block uncut: the seven northern portions are Dan, Asher, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, Reuben and Judah, each verse closing on the one-portion refrain. The doubled close it argues from at MT 47:23 is true with its mark class correctly distinguished from MT 48:29, and a paseq is indeed recorded within MT 48:1 and within MT 48:7.
items.both_sides: MT 47:23 side: the utterance signature and a closed-section mark stand in the same verse, and the topic turns from border-division instruction to the portion list itself. MT 48:7/48:8 side: MT 48:7 closes the northern block on the refrain and no mark stands at that seam, while MT 48:8 reopens with the same border frame the list uses at MT 48:2-7 and changes only its predicate, which is continuity evidence at that seam the row does not weigh. Two observations do not change the verdict. The list heading at MT 48:1 is called the list's own onset device in the rationale while the same verse's evidence field records no formula device; that is loose rather than false if the narrower phrase means the registered onset formulae only, and the byte-identical form opens MT 48:30, where it is treated as no device. And the rejected alternative's ground that a 29-verse span exceeds every cap is not supported by the ruled cap posture, which admits whole-chapter spans of 31 and 36 verses at reduced confidence with a cap disclosure. Neither point touches a Hebrew or Masoretic fact, so the row is supported.

suggested_fix.fact: the byte-identical list heading opens both MT 48:1 and MT 48:30, so it is an onset device at both places or at neither; and the ruled cap posture admits spans longer than 29 verses, so exceeding a cap is not available as the ground for rejecting a single undivided row

items.claim: Five ketiv/qere verses fall inside MT 48:8-48:22, at MT 48:14, 48:15, 48:16, 48:18 and 48:21, and the row discloses none of them. The corpus rule is that a row whose span covers a textual-variant site discloses it, and this is the largest such gap in the book, while the sibling row covering the river vision discloses all four of its own.
items.both_sides: MT 48:7/48:8 onset side: MT 48:7 closes the northern refrain block on the one-portion formula and no mark stands at the seam, while MT 48:8 reuses the list's own border frame and changes only the predicate, from a named portion to the offering. The seam therefore rests on a change of listed object, which the row labels accurately as carrying no formula device, though the frame's continuation is counter-evidence it does not state. MT 48:22/48:23 close side: no mark stands there either. The closed-section mark inside the span, recorded after MT 48:11, is correctly disclosed as mid-row and non-cutting, and no boundary is argued from any variant site. The cut holds; what is missing is disclosure of the five variant sites the span covers.

items.claim: The onset at MT 48:23 is argued from what the row calls an explicit resumption formula, but the opening words are a noun phrase meaning the remainder of the tribes, which is not a registered onset device; that form stands in two verses of the book only, MT 34:18 and MT 48:23, so it is not a recurring formula, and no parashah mark stands at MT 48:22. The row covering MT 48:8-48:22 calls this same seam formula-free, so the cluster carries two contradictory grounds for one seam.
items.both_sides: MT 48:22 side: the prince's land closes between Judah's and Benjamin's borders, with a paseq recorded inside the verse and no parashah mark at the seam. MT 48:23 side: the portion list resumes lexically, repeating from MT 48:1 the same word for the tribes and returning to the one-portion refrain. That is a real content seam and a lexical resumption head, but not a device of the registered onset classes. The cut at MT 48:23 holds on content and the span keeps the ruled refrain block MT 48:23-27 uncut, with the five southern portions Benjamin, Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun and Gad correct on the bytes and the open-section mark with the utterance at MT 48:29 correctly distinguished from the closed-section mark at MT 47:23. Only the ground asserted for the onset needs restating.

suggested_fix.fact: MT 48:23 opens with a lexical list-resumption head rather than a registered onset formula, and no parashah mark stands at MT 48:22, so that seam is formula-free

items.claim: The absent mark after MT 48:35 is given a reason, that none is possible on the book's last verse, and the witness does not support that reason. Marks stand freely on chapter-final verses here: 39 of the book's 48 chapter-final verses carry one, and MT 43:27 carries two consecutive closed-section marks. What the witness supports is only that none is recorded after MT 48:35.
items.both_sides: MT 48:29 side: the utterance signature and an open-section mark stand in the same verse and close the portion list; that is true, though it is argued in prose without appearing among the row's own cited refs. MT 48:30 side: no mark stands there, and the verse opens with the same heading form as MT 48:1, so the seam rests on the turn to the city's gates. The span is right on the bytes, with four sides measured and three gates each at MT 48:30-34 and the circumference and new name at MT 48:35, and the paseq inside MT 48:35 is recorded and correctly held to a count with no position claimed. Only the stated reason for the closing absence needs narrowing to what is recorded.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Five read-forms in these rows are rendered with the source's morpheme separator stripped and are not substrings of the running text: the read form after the northward-facing rooms at MT 46:19, and the read forms at MT 47:8, MT 47:10, MT 47:11 and MT 47:12. The witness's apparatus carries each with its separator, and in three of the five the written form is separated as well. Recorded as sites; the non-witness strings are deliberately not reproduced here.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: Whether this rendering is a sanctioned corpus convention is already routed and is not settled here. The automatic normalizer buckets read forms as their own class and reports no defect over this corpus, so it cannot settle the question either. If the convention is not sanctioned, five quotations in this cluster are strings the witness does not contain; if it is, nothing changes. Every other Hebrew run in these rows collates exactly.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Paseq occurrences are under-enumerated across this whole cluster, not in one row only: one within each of MT 48:2 through MT 48:6 unnamed by the northern-portions row, one within MT 48:18 and three within MT 48:21 unnamed by the holy-portion row, one each within MT 48:24, MT 48:25 and MT 48:26 unnamed by the southern-portions row, and one each within MT 47:16 and MT 47:17 unnamed by the border row.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: This is a book-wide pattern rather than a defect of these rows: about a third of the occurrences the corpus covers go unnamed, across 25 rows. It reads as an unstated convention that a paseq is named only where it bears on a seam. No boundary in this cluster rests on one, and the count-only treatment is correct wherever it is stated, so it should be settled as a convention rather than repaired row by row.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Two of the seven rows carry a different writer attempt identifier from the other five, inside the same part.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: Provenance only, and outside this lens; noted because the two rows concerned are the ones carrying the variant-site disclosure gap and the contradictory seam ground, so a single authoring pass may account for both.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The ground that a 29-verse undivided row would exceed every cap, used to reject the single-row alternative for this chapter, is not supported by the ruled cap posture, which admits longer whole-chapter spans at reduced confidence with a cap disclosure.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: It is the load-bearing reason given for three of the four cuts in this chapter. Those cuts have independent content grounds and the point is not a Hebrew or Masoretic question, so it is recorded rather than decided by this lens.

e19_selfreport: I ran no listing, no glob and no recursive search: not against my output directory, not against the worktree, and not against my own scratch. Every file was opened by the exact path given in my brief, my launch message or my own global policy, plus the ledger named in the authority paragraph. Self-checks were digests and content reads of named files only; no directory was ever tested for. My private scratch is a uniquely named subdirectory of my own session scratchpad, and I wrote nothing beneath the worktree and no receipt.
limit: one lens on one cluster; candidate-only, non-authorizing research review
